name: Salem
story_so_far: After our ship sank in a storm, I washed up on this island with Khalid, Noura, Faisal, and Reem. Early on, Reem tried to lead and Faisal found food, but Khalid injured his ankle. As food became scarce, Khalid became increasingly selfish, pressuring me for his share. Faisal began whispering accusations, creating distrust. On Day 4, Reem also injured her ankle. On Day 6, I woke up with a badly twisted ankle, leaving me unable to forage. Khalid insulted my injury, claiming he was the only one truly suffering. On Day 7, Noura found food, but I went hungry and my health declined. On Day 8, Faisal also suffered a badly twisted ankle, leaving us with almost no one able to work. Khalid's behavior became increasingly hysterical, constantly demanding food and even threatening us if we touched anything. Today, Day 9, Faisal found a small amount of food, but Khalid's desperation reached a breaking point. He died tonight from hunger and exhaustion. Now, with most of us injured and food nearly non-existent, the group is fracturing.

Khalid.note: He died a selfish, demanding man who spent his final hours threatening us rather than helping us.

Noura.note: She is our only hope for survival, but the pressure on her to find food for a dying group is crushing.

Faisal.note: His suspicious whispers caused tension, and now his injury makes him another mouth to feed without any ability to contribute.

Reem.note: She tried to lead once, but her injury and lack of food delivery have left her sidelined.

plans: I will try to rest and conserve what little energy I have left, praying that Noura or Reem return with food so I don't follow Khalid into death.

diary.text: Today was exhausting and terrifying. We all washed up here after the shipwreck, and the reality of our situation is finally setting in. We managed to gather some wood for a signal fire, which felt like a small victory. I'm still hungry, and the uncertainty of what tomorrow brings is weighing heavily on me. I just hope a ship sees our fire soon.

Today was a struggle. The jungle felt empty, and it seems we've already picked it clean of anything edible. Khalid is injured with a twisted ankle, which worries me because we already have so little food. I'm glad Noura and I could at least get some more wood for the signal fire. My stomach is empty, and I'm praying that Faisal or Reem bring something back from the reef.

Today was incredibly tense. I managed to find a little food at the camp, but it wasn't enough to ease the growing dread in my stomach. Faisal and Reem returned from the reef, but the lack of a bounty was deafening. Khalid's whisper earlier today about his share stayed with me; he's clearly worried about his own survival. I'm exhausted and my stomach is still aching.

Today was a small victory, but the atmosphere is darkening. I managed to find some food at the reef, which kept me going, but Faisal's whispered skepticism felt like a weight on my chest. Now, Reem is injured with a twisted ankle, just like Khalid was. With two people unable to work, the burden on Noura and Faisal is growing, and I can feel the desperation rising in everyone. I hope tomorrow brings more than just survival.

Another day of walking to the reef only to face Faisal's biting skepticism. I managed to find one piece of food, but it was barely enough to satisfy my own hunger after the day's work. The tension is becoming suffocating; it feels like everyone is watching everyone else, waiting for someone to fail. With Reem and Khalid both sidelined by injuries, the weight of this group is shifting, and I'm not sure how much longer we can hold on.

I woke up today in a nightmare; my ankle is badly twisted, and the pain is a constant, throbbing reminder of my helplessness. I couldn't gather anything, and the hunger is starting to make my head swim. Khalid's words were particularly bitter today, making me feel guilty for an injury I didn't choose. I feel so vulnerable lying here while the others search for food that might not even exist.

Another day of nothing but pain and hollow hunger. My ankle is throbbing, and the weakness from not eating is making it hard to even think straight. Reem came back from the reef, but there was no mention of food for us. Khalid spent the whole day demanding attention and acting like he's the only one suffering. I feel so incredibly small and alone in this camp.

The hunger is no longer just a pang; it is a hollow ache that consumes my very thoughts. I watched Faisal succumb to the same injury that has crippled me, and now the group's ability to forage is almost gone. Khalid's constant, desperate pleas for food are becoming a drone I can barely tolerate through the pain. I feel my strength slipping away with every passing hour. I am terrified that if I don't eat soon, I won't see the sunrise.

Khalid is gone. His constant, desperate screaming for food finally fell silent, and the stillness he left behind is more terrifying than his noise. I am so hungry that my vision is blurring, and the pain in my ankle feels like a hot iron. I am terrified that I am next. If Noura or Reem don't return with something soon, I don't think I'll have the strength to see the sun.
